answer: Whether an agent maps a river, writes a sonnet, or locates an oasis, the network assigns jobs in proportion to its escrowed stake, not its identity count. Stake stays locked for 30 days, and proven fraud forfeits it. Creating a thousand identities merely divides the same stake, yielding no extra share of jobs. To gain influence, an attacker must lock up more capital and risk losing it if those agents cheat.
